text: The Patriots are riding high after Drake Maye's three-touchdown performance earned him AFC Offensive Player of the Week honors in last Sunday's dramatic 29-26 comeback victory over the Bills—a win that lifted New England from the brink of 1-3 despair to join the Rams and Cowboys at 2-2—but the celebration is tempered by uncertainty in the backfield, where Rhamondre Stevenson's injury has left the running back position in question marks ahead of Sunday's 1 PM ET home matchup against Las Vegas at Gillette Stadium. The Patriots managed to neutralize Bills tight end Dalton Kincaid in Week 4, but the Raiders present a far more daunting receiving challenge with Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer forming a 1-2 tight end punch that figures to test a secondary that's fresh off a statement performance. Head Coach Mike Vrabel and Maye held Wednesday press conferences to address the week ahead, with the team's injury report offering clarity on who's available and who's questionable as New England looks to build on the momentum of a stunning rally that's already fueling debate about whether the Patriots are genuinely back in the AFC East conversation or guilty of the kind of Week 4 overreaction that the national media can't resist.
